title: Technical Report OFDM-Assisted Simultaneous Quantum and Classical THz Communications
authors: Xin Liu, Chao Xu, Soon Xin Ng, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Phuc V. Trinh, Shinya Sugiura, Lajos Hanzo
abstract: The feasibility of cost-effective simultaneous quantum and classical communication (SQCC) transmitting both the quantum key and classical information via a superimposed coherent state is investigated both in optical and Terahertz (THz) bands. Since the existing THz SQCC schemes assume single-carrier (SC) transmission over flat fading channels, we embark on investigating SQCC in realistic frequency-selective multipath THz fading channels. We then propose an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based SQCC system for time-invariant frequency-selective THz scenarios, supported by low-density parity-check coded (LDPC) multidimensional QKD reconciliation schemes. Our simulation results demonstrate that the OFDM-based SQCC scheme is capable of achieving a practical secret key rate (SKR) over a wide range of power sharing scenarios between the classical and quantum signals. By contrast its single-carrier counterpart requires the classical signal to be at least 100 times stronger than the quantum signal in THz SQCC.
summary: This paper proposes an OFDM-based system for Simultaneous Quantum and Classical Communication (SQCC) in challenging THz frequency-selective fading channels. By processing signals in the frequency domain, the OFDM scheme maintains a practical Secret Key Rate across various power allocations. This significantly improves performance compared to single-carrier methods, making THz quantum communication more viable.
main_problem: The paper investigates the feasibility of cost-effective Simultaneous Quantum and Classical Communication (SQCC) in realistic, frequency-selective multipath Terahertz (THz) fading channels.
main_result: The proposed Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) based SQCC scheme achieves a practical Secret Key Rate (SKR) over various power sharing scenarios, significantly outperforming its single-carrier counterpart.
method: The authors propose an OFDM-based protocol that superimposes classical and quantum signals in the frequency domain, utilizing LDPC coded reconciliation schemes.
model_or_system: The system operates in the THz band, modeling the channel as frequency-selective multipath fading. The protocol involves superimposing classical BPSK signals with Gaussian Modulated (GM) CV-QKD signals.
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR), Bit Error Rate (BER), and Block Error Rate (BLER).
important_parameters: Power sharing ratio ($\zeta = P_Q/P_C$), Ricean factor ($K$), and the channel fading characteristics (frequency-selective).
main_assumptions: The investigation focuses on multipath-induced channel dispersion, treating beamforming as a link-enabling mechanism, and using LDPC CV-QKD reconciliation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase-space representations of the signals, protocol diagrams for SC and OFDM approaches, and plots showing SKR vs. distance, and BLER vs. power sharing ratio ($\zeta$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the SQCC protocol by first establishing the time-domain (SC) approach, then extending it to the frequency-domain using OFDM, and finally analyzing the performance metrics like SKR and BLER under varying power sharing ratios.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum communication in a high-frequency, complex channel regime (THz), which is a major frontier in quantum optics and quantum networks, requiring advanced signal processing techniques like OFDM.
